### Problem

The organisation's required pull request workflow (`org-pull-request.yml`, the ruleset's workflow rule in every repository) calls `waiting-update.yml`, whose `view` job ("The "What waits" view") runs in the concurrency group `waiting-view-<repository>` with `cancel-in-progress: true`. When several pull requests of one repository get events at once (a batch of updates, merges or reruns), each run cancels the view of the one before, those required runs end `cancelled`, and the ruleset blocks their merge. A batch rerun cancels itself again; only reruns one at a time go green. Seen on 2026-11-23 in DiluxOne/diluxone-fm: runs 45212132175, 45212140373, 45212146700 and 45212192369 (cancelled twice, then success) held #314, #315, #316 and #328, and earlier the same day #987/#988/#990/#992 here showed UNSTABLE from cancelled view jobs. The view is an organisation-wide page that `waiting-digest.yml` and the issues workflow also rewrite: whether one of its runs was replaced says nothing about the pull request. Note that `cancel-in-progress: false` alone does not fix it: GitHub keeps one pending run per group and cancels the others.

### Scope

- A replaced or superseded run of the "What waits" view never makes the pull request's required workflow fail, be cancelled or block a merge.
- The view stays up to date after pull request events (one rewrite after a burst is enough).

### Out of scope

- What the view lists and how it groups it.
- The per-item board update (`update` job), which already queues one run per item.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given three pull requests of one repository whose required workflow runs at the same time, when their view jobs overlap, then each required workflow concludes success (or fails only for its own checks), and none is cancelled.
- C2: Given a burst of pull request events, when it settles, then the "What waits" issue is rewritten at least once after the last event.
- C3: Given a pull request with a failing check of its own, when its required workflow runs, then it still fails as today.

### Criticality

Normal
